correctness.rationale: Fresh Bernoulli edge snapshots yield block transition matrix P=[[r^b I_a,(1-r^b)/b J],[(1-r^a)/a J,r^a I_b]], because exchangeability makes each neighbor equally likely conditional on moving. Eigenvalues are 1, r^a+r^b-1, r^b multiplicity a-1 and r^a multiplicity b-1. The spectral Kemeny identity gives (a-1)/q_b+(b-1)/q_a+1/(q_a+q_b), with q_k=1-r^k. Convex-decreasing f(x)=1/(1-r^x) and symmetry show strict minimum at balanced parts. The absolute radius is max(r^a,1-r^a-r^b) for a<=b; its opposing monotone branches yield the exact star/balanced/crossover alternatives, including star at p=1/2,n>=5. For balanced K_m,m, the negative near-minus-one part-constant eigenvalue bounds TV mixing below by (log2)/[-log(1-2^(1-m))], while star radius 1/2 gives TV<=2(1/2)^t and mixing by t=3. Kemeny balanced ~2m, star ~4m. Independent direct transition-matrix spectral computations for 474 (n,a,p) instances n=4..18 verified formulas and extrema; small near-ties were excluded from floating comparison, and exact proofs cover all n and 0<p<1.

value.rationale: Stationary-target average hitting times and worst-start mixing are standard but importantly different objectives in stochastic networks. An exact all-order tradeoff—balanced graph has half the asymptotic Kemeny but exponential mixing delay versus star—is a mathematically motivated counterexample to identifying their optimizers.
